original_value: Hyperspectral remote sensing is based on measuring the scattered and reflected electromagnetic signals from the Earth’s surface emitted by the Sun. The received radiance at the sensor is usually degraded by atmospheric effects and instrumental (sensor) noises which include thermal (Johnson) noise, quantization noise, and shot (photon) noise. Noise reduction is often considered as a preprocessing step for hyperspectral imagery. In the past decade, hyperspectral noise reduction techniques have evolved substantially from two dimensional bandwise techniques to three dimensional ones, and varieties of low-rank methods have been forwarded to improve the signal to noise ratio of the observed data. Despite all the developments and advances, there is a lack of a comprehensive overview of these techniques and their impact on hyperspectral imagery applications. In this paper, we address the following two main issues; (1) Providing an overview of the techniques developed in the past decade for hyperspectral image noise reduction; (2) Discussing the performance of these techniques by applying them as a preprocessing step to improve a hyperspectral image analysis task, i.e., classification. Additionally, this paper discusses about the hyperspectral image modeling and denoising challenges. Furthermore, different noise types that exist in hyperspectral images have been described. The denoising experiments have confirmed the advantages of the use of low-rank denoising techniques compared to the other denoising techniques in terms of signal to noise ratio and spectral angle distance. In the classification experiments, classification accuracies have improved when denoising techniques have been applied as a preprocessing step.

result.paraphrase: Hyperspectral remote sensing relies on measuring the Sun’s electromagnetic signals scattered from and reflected by the Earth’s surface. At the sensor, the received radiance is typically degraded by atmospheric effects and instrumental noise, including thermal (Johnson), quantization, and shot (photon) noise. Noise reduction is commonly treated as a preprocessing step for hyperspectral imagery. Over the past decade, hyperspectral denoising methods have advanced markedly from two-dimensional bandwise approaches to three-dimensional ones, and many low-rank techniques have been proposed to improve the signal-to-noise ratio of observed data. Even with these developments, there is still no comprehensive overview of these methods and their effects on hyperspectral image applications. In this paper, we tackle two main problems: first, we survey the techniques developed over the last decade for hyperspectral image noise reduction; second, we evaluate their performance by using them as a preprocessing step to improve a hyperspectral image analysis task, namely classification. The paper also discusses hyperspectral image modeling and denoising challenges, and describes the different noise types present in hyperspectral images. Denoising experiments confirm that low-rank methods outperform other denoising techniques in terms of signal-to-noise ratio and spectral angle distance. Classification experiments likewise show improved accuracies when denoising is applied as a preprocessing step.
